business_problem: 1Password needed to compress the time between planning and production, reduce investigation and review overhead, and expand builder capacity without weakening the company's zero-knowledge security posture.
solution_summary: 1Password embedded Codex across planning, implementation, review, testing, release readiness, and incident investigation so engineering work can move from user story to production with fewer handoffs. Codex turns requests into specs, dependency checks, and work items; helps engineers navigate Rust and TypeScript code through the CLI; reviews pull requests before humans; runs acceptance criteria and tests in parallel; and investigates live defects by pulling evidence from telemetry, source control, paging, feature flags, and incident systems. The company also wrapped Codex inside its internal AppSec harness and secret-reference model so credentials are resolved only at execution time and never exposed in model context. That combination let 1Password speed up feature delivery, ship internal tools such as Knox and an AI SRE agent, and extend builder workflows into finance and marketing without trading away core security controls.

data_flow: User stories and requests enter Codex, which breaks them into specs, code changes, tests, and review steps. During execution, Codex can query telemetry, paging, feature flags, and source control to investigate problems, while the AppSec harness and secret-reference workflow inject credentials only at the point of action so secure outputs flow back into engineering review.
business_outcome: 1Password measured a 20.9% productivity improvement, a 10.9% reduction in median PR cycle time, roughly 90% faster investigation of a multi-service production issue, and a modeled 553% ROI from engineering capacity gains.
